And like right now it seems most of the street bands, most of the bands play, I mean you know, like, without sheet music, whereas they used to play sheet music and by number.

Yeah, well you see, the by number thing which you're talking about, you see years ago the older musicians, you know like they had some good brass bands years ago when I was a kid, like the Imperial Brass Band, and they had and they had and Red Allen Brass Band from Across the River, the Tuxedo Brass Band with Celestan, or they had some fine brass bands, and they all had music. And if they hire a man to play in a band, what they used to do, put the name of the piece of music off and use the number. Them that didn't have a number, they put a number on it and say, let's play such and such a number. And if you could, well, if you didn't hear you, they know you wouldn't read that music, they don't hire no more. So that's the way it was. Because all the good brass bands, I would say the good ones, because they had a couple other brass bands that were just going on and playing, you know, but the good brass bands. Well now you see, we play these numbers so many times and so often we don't need the music for it ourselves, you know. Only the time I pull music out for the band, it's like, oh sometimes we play a big funeral and I want to play, you know, so you might ask for a request. Like if Larry Bernstein around him is special, he can ask for West Long. So I usually carry that with me when he's going to be around, you know. Or a couple others, you know, like Flea as a Boyd or something like that, according to how long the funeral is, so you add some of these beautiful, pretty music in it, you know, because I think all the funeral drives are so beautiful. Yeah. Yeah, I do. That's why I love to play the funeral. And if you pay attention to me when I'm playing the funeral, you'll see some tears rolling down my cheeks, you know.
Yeah, that's one thing that I at least miss nowadays is very few bands can play dirges.

Yeah, that's right. And if you play the odds, you don't play them right. Right. And then that's why sometimes if it's a big, big funeral, I've got some numbers there. I've got some beautiful funeral times, you know, like Flea as a Boyd, West Long, and one we call the, Ricky's called the Blimp, but it's number 31, though, you know, just called the Blimp. I don't know, I never did know the name of it. Yeah, I've got some beautiful funeral dies, but the man that's got the funeral dies is Percy Humphrey. Every now and then I try to get one from him, and he'd give me an excuse. I don't know why, but that's just the way the old timers used to be, you know. They had some beautiful funeral dies, and then all that wasn't playing, and they didn't care about no other band playing it, because they didn't get all the glory when they playing it, you know. It wasn't, not the question of being mean or nothing, just one of them things, that's the way they did.

I believe some time ago you said that the, you know, from what I read in the jazz archives, the interview in jazz archives, you said that the parade music had actually gotten worse.

And you attributed it to the, I suppose, the bass drum, the drummers aren't as good. Well, no, no, they're not as good as the drummers used to be. Oh. I got a drummer, his daddy was, oh, his daddy was a, was a drummer, Brooker T. Henry Glass, get him. And, uh, so he, uh, the reason, I guess the reason why he played like he played, not because he was following behind his dad since he was a little bitty thing, you know, holding on his daddy's coat tail while his daddy was playing the bass drums. And, uh, that's probably why he's good as he is. But, uh, they had some good bass drummers at one time, you know, like the Nestor Pange and Lil Jim and Ock and them, a bunch of them, you know. Like Henry Glass was calling Booker T and Sun Fu Klo, which is a little to Eureka. And had some pretty good bass drummers, but after them good bass drummers died, I, just like I said, you know, you're a fine, you're kind of on one hand. Yeah.
You know, when you were talking to me over the phone you said sometimes you play three funerals in one day.
Yeah.
I have a hard time believing that because I used to remember funerals that would last about four hours. Oh, some funerals would last five or six hours.

It would last four hours. I don't see how you could play three in one day. Yeah. You see, the Catholic funerals never last long. Oh. You see, if you get two Catholic funerals in the morning and one o'clock, maybe one, two o'clock, you're playing a Baptist or Protestant funeral, well you'd probably be in the street until six, seven o'clock. But you get through them Catholic funerals in no time. Now sometimes you catch a Baptist funeral that the fellow never belonged to no church and they dismiss them right from the house. Well now they really have the funeral procession at the church at night and they just dismiss the next day. But one time if a fellow didn't belong to no church or nothing and the preacher didn't want to do no lying about him or nothing, they just would dismiss him from the house, you know. And so sometimes you catch a Catholic, a Baptist, and maybe two Baptists, you see. Yeah, I played three a day already. And two a day was common. But you see it all the time, I go for that little dollar and a half, two rounds, and then if you went to three dollars, you're making three dollars of man, you were raising hell. So we'd live from Al Jays to Walkatown, man. And then on the way of coming back, you'd play a parade. Yeah, stop that. I stopped that. You know, I told them, I said, no, one way. Two ways, I charge them double price, that's all. Yeah, but man, one time they had to pass the man in front of his door. And bar him where he used to bump, might be six blocks away, had to go pass in front of that bar room. Then you had to go to the graveyard, if the graveyard was walking distance, sometimes you had to turn them loose before you hit the graveyard. Then coming back, they're making a parade all around where he used to bump at and all like that. Four or five hours wasn't nothing for a funeral one time. Yeah, I played them.
